brief: Goldman Prime Brokerage reports a historic hedge fund de-grossing. On Thursday (Oct 22), the GS VIP-longs-vs-most-shorted-names basket (GSTHVIPP) finished down about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011, leaving it down 10.4% month-to-date; the only larger single-day drop on record was -8.26% on August 8, 2011, the day after S&P downgraded the US. The same day, Fundamental L/S funds fell 1.1%, Systematic funds 1.2% and Multi-Strats 1.4%, the first time since Covid all three strategies lost more than 1% on the same day. Hedge funds have de-grossed in 7 of the past 8 sessions, an accelerating pace last seen in April 2026 and absent throughout 2025. Thursday itself was the year's 5th-largest de-grossing event (-1.6 sigma), driven entirely by long selling, the largest since September 2025. The unwind spanned North America, Europe and EM Asia (China and Hong Kong hit hardest) and 9 of 11 global sectors, led by Info Tech (largest net selling since September 2024, driven by Semi & Semi Equipment) and Industrials. Global AI names saw their largest net selling since end of July. Prime book gross leverage fell 0.4pts to 312.3% and net leverage fell 2.1pts to 71.8%.
